pack.title: First Steps
pack.description: From the dojo to the city market: hiragana and katakana, greetings on the road, and ordering tea.

items.usage: The everyday daytime greeting. The final は is read "wa".
Evening greeting. The final は is read "wa".
A parting for someone you may not see again soon.
Said to someone setting off on a journey.

items.text: どこから{来|き}ましたか。
{京都|きょうと}から{来|き}ました。

example.text: このおにぎりはおいしいです。

items.usage: Said after naming what you want, or when asking a favor.
Said with your hands together right before you start eating or drinking.
Said when you meet someone for the first time, usually followed by your name.
Calls a server over, apologizes lightly, or thanks someone who went out of their way.

items.text: ありがとうございます
items.usage: The polite thank-you for staff, strangers and anyone older than you.
Shop and restaurant staff say this when you walk in. Customers don't say it back; a nod is enough.
Said after finishing a meal: to the cook, your host, or the staff as you leave.

items.notes: Name the thing, then を (said "o"), then ください.

items.text: お{茶|ちゃ}を{一|ひと}つください。
{注文|ちゅうもん}をお{願|ねが}いします。
お{会計|かいけい}をお{願|ねが}いします。

choices.feedback: Greet back with the same words.
That's for the morning; the sun is setting.

{京都|きょうと}へ{行|い}きます。

Place, へ (to, read "e"), {行|い}きます (go).

dialogues.title: Ordering at the café
dialogues.setting: A small café by the station, mid-morning

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: すみません、{注文|ちゅうもん}をお{願|ねが}いします。
lines.en: Excuse me, I'd like to order.

choices.text: すみません、{注文|ちゅうもん}をお{願|ねが}いします。

choices.feedback: You say that right before eating, not to ask for something.
That is for meeting someone for the first time.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: お{茶|ちゃ}を{一|ひと}つください。

choices.text: お{茶|ちゃ}を{一|ひと}つください。
choices.feedback: The thing, を, how many, ください. Perfect.
That means 'It is tea', not a request.
That is what you say after a meal.

lines.speaker: clerk
lines.text: かしこまりました。{少々|しょうしょう}お{待|ま}ちください。

lines.speaker: clerk
lines.text: お{待|ま}たせしました。お{茶|ちゃ}です。
lines.en: Sorry to keep you waiting. Your tea.

lines.text: ありがとうございます。

choices.text: ありがとうございます。

choices.feedback: Said right before eating or drinking.
That one comes after you finish.

note.title: Five vowels
note.body: Every kana is one beat. The five vowels are short and crisp: a as in 'father', i as in 'see', u as in 'food' with relaxed lips, e as in 'get', o as in 'old' but short.

nodes.title: The K row かきくけこ

note.title: Add a k
note.body: Put a k in front of each vowel: か ka, き ki, く ku, け ke, こ ko. Same rhythm, one beat each.

note.title: The second script
note.body: Katakana are the same sounds as hiragana in a sharper, straighter hand: ア a, イ i, ウ u, エ e, オ o. A samurai reads both.

note.title: Sharp k-sounds
note.body: カ ka, キ ki, ク ku, ケ ke, コ ko. Compare them with か き く け こ: same sounds, straighter strokes.

note.title: Greet by the time of day
note.body: おはようございます in the morning, こんにちは in the day, こんばんは in the evening. The は at the end of こんにちは and こんばんは is read "wa".

note.title: から means "from"
note.body: Put から after a place: {京都|きょうと}から = from Kyoto. {来|き}ました means "came". Ask with どこ (where): どこから{来|き}ましたか。

note.title: へ means "to"
note.body: へ after a place marks where you are headed. As a particle it is read "e": {江戸|えど}へ{行|い}きます = I am going to Edo. Travellers part with {気|き}をつけて (take care).

note.title: Someone on the road
note.body: A pilgrim stops to talk. Greet them, say where you came from and where you are going.

note.title: を + ください
note.body: Say the thing, then を (pronounced "o"), then ください: {水|みず}をください means "water, please".

note.title: いただきます
note.body: Hands together, a small nod, then いただきます: it thanks everyone who brought the meal to you.

exercises.scene: Your food has just arrived and you are about to eat.
You have just named the cake you want. Add "please".

note.title: すみません does a lot
note.body: すみません means "excuse me" and "sorry". In a café it is how you call the server over.

exercises.scene: You meet your host family for the first time.
You want the server to come to your table.
You have finished eating and are getting up to leave.

note.title: Counting things
note.body: {一|ひと}つ (one) and {二|ふた}つ (two) count things in general. The number goes after を: お{茶|ちゃ}を{一|ひと}つください。

note.title: なん before です
note.body: Before です, {何|なん} is read なん: これは{何|なん}ですか。

exercises.scene: You sit down and want to see what they have.
You take a bite and love it.
You are finished and want to pay.

note.title: Your first order
note.body: Listen to the clerk and choose what you say. Everything here is something you already know.

exercises.text: お{茶|ちゃ}＿＿{一|ひと}つください。

exercises.scene: Your meal has just been served.
